newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. says agencies cheated job seekers.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. says agencies cheated job seekers.

text.p: City authorities closed two employment agencies and charged more than 20 others for cheating unskilled job seekers by illegally demanding upfront fees, a consumer affairs official said on Tuesday.

"We think it's basically unfair because these are people who are trying to stay off welfare and trying to do the right thing, don't have much money to start with and $100 is a huge fee to them," said Pat Cohen, spokeswoman for the New York City Department of Consumer Affairs.
"Agencies are allowed to take upfront fees in this category of lower skilled jobs but they have to send you on interviews ... they can't just keep the money."
Consumer Affairs Commissioner Jose Maldonado will announce Wednesday charges against 26 employment agencies accused of levying the fees and operating without a license, Cohen said.
She said 90 percent of the agencies inspected by the department were found to be breaking the law by charging the $100 fee to workers who were seeking household-cleaning and restaurant work.
